## Diagnosis

Running `python reproduce.py` exposed a crash: an `Invar::Invariant` with **"bad bond stereo"**, thrown from `Canon.cpp:362` in `canonicalizeDoubleBond` (a `PRECONDITION` that a double bond with `stereo > STEREOANY` must carry ≥2 stereo atoms).

The supplied V3000 input is an **enamide** `CH3-CH=CH-NH-C(=O)-CH3` (7 atoms, an E C=C double bond + a wedged amide C–N single bond). It loads and serializes fine, but `TautomerEnumerator::canonicalize` fails.

**Root cause:** During parsing, the amide C–N single bond is incorrectly assigned an atropisomer flag (`STEREOATROPCW`). In `TautomerEnumerator::setTautomerStereoAndIsoHs`, when a tautomer transform converts that single bond into a C=N double bond (amide → imide tautomer), the stereo-preservation branch (active because the probe sets `setRemoveBondStereo(false)`) blindly copied the single-bond atropisomer flag onto the new **double** bond. That left a double bond with a stereo flag but **0 stereo atoms** — exactly the malformed state that trips the precondition in `canonicalizeDoubleBond`. Atropisomer flags are only meaningful on single bonds.

## The fix

In `source/Code/GraphMol/MolStandardize/Tautomer.cpp` (`setTautomerStereoAndIsoHs`), when preserving bond stereo on an unchanged-order bond, I now drop an atropisomer flag (`STEREOATROPCW`/`STEREOATROPCCW`) — resetting it to `STEREONONE` and clearing stereo atoms — instead of carrying it onto a double bond. Everything else (the `modified` bookkeeping, E/Z/CIS/TRANS preservation with their stereo atoms, and direction copying) is byte-identical to the original, so this is maximally surgical.
